title: NY State Assembly · District 59
area: Brooklyn: Canarsie, Flatlands, Georgetown, Mill Basin, Marine Park, Bergen Beach, and Gerritsen Beach

context.text: Incumbent Jaime Williams (D) defeated Jibreel Jalloh 66.0% to 33.8% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Jalloh remains on the November ballot on the Working Families Party line, so the general election is a rematch between the two.

candidates.name: Jaime Williams
candidates.currentRole: NY State Assembly Member, District 59 (since May 2016)

summary.text: Jaime Williams is the incumbent Democratic and Conservative Party candidate for Assembly District 59, first elected in a 2016 special election. She chairs the Assembly's Real Property Taxation Committee and defeated primary challenger Jibreel Jalloh in June 2026.

background.text: Williams holds a bachelor's degree in social work from York College and a master's degree in social work from Fordham University, and later earned a CASAC-T certificate (Credentialed Alcoholism and Substance Abuse Counselor) from Kingsborough Community College.
She has more than eight years of experience counseling women and children who were victims of domestic violence, and clients who were HIV-positive with a history of substance abuse.

She served as Community Project Director for Brooklyn East at Catholic Charities, providing outreach programs in Brownsville, East New York, Canarsie, and Mill Basin, and worked with Catholic Charities on relief efforts after Superstorm Sandy.
She is a past member of the 69th Precinct Community Council, the Mill Basin Civic Association, and Brooklyn Community Board 18, and is a member of NYC's Community Emergency Response Team (CERT).

positions.summary: Prime sponsor of two 2025-2026 bills that would discount or reimburse Manhattan central business district tolls for residents of designated 'transit deserts,' reducing the reach of the congestion pricing program.

record.text: Chairs the Assembly's Real Property Taxation Committee (2023-2024 and 2025-2026 sessions); also serves on the Agriculture, Environmental Conservation, Governmental Operations, and Transportation committees.

Prime sponsor of A03887, which would give a 50% discount on Manhattan central business district tolls, fees, and other congestion-pricing charges to residents of designated transit deserts; referred to the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee, no floor vote as of September 2026.

Prime sponsor of A03856, which would require the Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority to reimburse transit-desert residents 100% of central business district tolls when traveling for medical treatment or religious services; referred to committee, no floor vote as of September 2026.

candidates.name: Jibreel Jalloh
candidates.ballotNote: Lost the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary to incumbent Jaime Williams; remains on the November general-election ballot on the Working Families Party line.

summary.text: Jibreel Jalloh is a Brooklyn-born community organizer and nonprofit leader running for Assembly District 59 on the Working Families Party line after losing the Democratic primary to incumbent Jaime Williams.

background.text: Jalloh is the son of a union nurse and a taxi driver and was born and raised in Brooklyn.

He is described as an Obama Scholar, community organizer, and nonprofit leader; his campaign says he helped stop a toxic facility from being sited near homes and schools, helped secure $1.6 million in gun-violence prevention funding, and supported workers organizing a union.
He has also built and run a small business, according to his campaign.

priorities.text: "Lower the Cost of Living: Fund universal childcare, healthcare and expand access to fresh and affordable food."
"Protect Homeowners: Stop deed theft, expand foreclosure prevention programs, support first-time homebuyer grants."
"Economic investment & Small Businesses: Secure funding to revitalize our commercial corridors and push legislation that bolsters our small businesses."
"Invest in Education & Youth: Modernize school facilities, expand after-school and summer programs, and connect students to career and college pathways."
"Fix Flooding & Infrastructure: Upgrade drainage systems, expand green infrastructure, and create emergency relief for flood-impacted families. Fund NYCHA repairs."

candidates.researchNotes: Jalloh has never held elected office, so there is no official voting or bill-sponsorship record. His positions come from his campaign website, which lists issue priorities but does not take an explicit stance on gun-law policy, so no 'guns' position is included even though his materials mention gun-violence-prevention funding.

researchNotes: Jaime Williams has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey in any cycle and has no current campaign website; her recent nyassembly.gov press releases predate the 2025-2026 session, so no current-cycle 'priorities in their own words' statements could be found and researchDepth is marked 'basic' with her record documented from official committee, bill-sponsorship, and floor-vote sources instead.
